description: Practical technique cues and coordination drills. Practice choices, not diagnoses or validated corrections for pose angles.

activities.title: Fold, bring through, step down
activities.text: Let the knee fold as the thigh comes forward, then bring the foot down beneath you. Practise the connected action without deliberately stretching the foot farther ahead.

activities.title: Stay tall without stiffening
activities.text: Keep your head comfortably over your trunk. Let your shoulders stay relaxed as your arms alternate; avoid leaning backward to lift the knee.

activities.title: Sprint march
activities.text: Stand tall and alternate lifting a knee while the opposite arm comes forward. Let the knee fold naturally, then place the foot down beneath you. Keep the motion comfortable; slow down if your trunk starts rocking.

activities.title: Controlled step-up
activities.text: If already part of your strength routine, use a comfortable step height and keep the movement controlled. This is general strength practice; the video has not identified a weak muscle.

activities.title: Controlled squat
activities.text: Use a familiar, comfortable bodyweight squat from your existing routine. Keep the motion controlled. Treat this as general strength practice, not a correction prescribed from an angle.

activities.title: Let your arms alternate
activities.text: Let the arm opposite the forward leg come forward. Keep your hands loose and allow the elbows to bend and open naturally instead of locking them into a fixed angle.

activities.title: Step down without reaching
activities.text: Think about bringing the foot down beneath you rather than stretching it forward for a longer step. Do not deliberately force it behind your hips.

activities.title: Alternating arm march
activities.text: March comfortably in place with the opposite arm coming forward as each knee rises. Keep your hands loose and let your elbows change angle naturally. Slow down if you lose the alternating rhythm.

activities.title: Easy A-skip
activities.text: If A-skips are already familiar, use a gentle skipping rhythm with alternating knee lift and opposite-arm action. Stay tall and bring the foot down beneath you. Start with the sprint march if the rhythm feels awkward; keep this easy rather than trying for height or speed.
